label: Copper Price (LME) — 2026 COCHILCO Forecast
change: Copper closed at a new all-time high of US$6.736/lb (US$14,850/tonne) on Aug 17, 2026; on Sep 8–9 LME cash copper settled at US$14,737/tonne (+1.35%), its second-highest close on record behind the Aug 17 peak, as fears that new US tariffs on refined copper would 'wipe out the global surplus' met permitting delays and cost inflation in Chile and Peru — Chilean output fell 9.4% YoY in July after storm damage in the northern mining belt — alongside sustained Chinese grid and renewable-energy demand; Dipres projects a record US$8.04B in mining payments to the Treasury in 2026, with Diario Financiero estimating over US$9.7B in additional fiscal revenue versus the budget's US$4.38/lb reference price
source: London Metal Exchange / Dipres / Diario Financiero (Sep 2026)

label: GDP Growth Rate
change: The Central Bank's September 2026 Informe de Política Monetaria (IPoM) cut its 2026 growth forecast from 1%–1.75% to 0.25%–0.75%, citing weakening demand, a deteriorating labor market, falling business confidence and the drag from fuel-price increases; it projects a rebound to 2%–3% growth in 2027 and 2.25%–3.25% in 2028, aided by reconstruction-law spending. Unemployment reached 9.5% in the May–July quarter (~981,000 people) — the highest in five years and the highest in Latin America — six months into the Kast administration, up from 9.4% in Mar–May; IMACEC had contracted 1.5% YoY in July, the worst reading in over three years
source: Banco Central de Chile — IPoM September 2026 / INE

label: Annual Inflation (CPI)
change: August 2026 monthly CPI +0.6%, above the Central Bank's 3% target; food & non-alcoholic beverages +1.4%, transport +1.6%; 3.6% accumulated YTD, 4.1% over 12 months — up from 3.5% in July, pulling further from target as the IPoM flagged fuel-price effects on household income
